findings.issue: The MISSING_SALE repair only checks that the admin-entered amount is greater than zero. It has no upper bound, so one ADMIN or FINANCE user can book a SALE of up to 999,999,999,999.99 (the numeric(14,2) limit) on any shipment that order-service confirms as DELIVERED for that seller. That SALE then goes out in the next payout run. This is a new way to create seller balance with no second check. The durable audit record does not capture the amount either. AuditInterceptor builds its 'after' payload from request.getRequestURI(), which leaves out the query string, so audit.events shows only 'POST /api/admin/ledger/discrepancies/{id}/repair 200' with no amount. The amount survives only in the app log and in the editable detail column of the same table. A value above the column limit raises a DataAccessException, not an ApplicationException, so the caller gets a 500 and no WARN line records the actor.
findings.fix: Limit the amount to the register value. Reject with 409 when the amount is more than d.expected(), the register amount stored on the row (or allow a small configured tolerance), and log the refusal at WARN with the actor. A larger amount should need a separate, explicitly audited path or a second approver. Also put the amount in the audit event: either publish a dedicated audit record from repair() with resourceId, actor, amount and the register amount, or have AuditInterceptor include the query string for this route. Check the precision before calling recordDelivered (amount.setScale(2) must be > 0 and below 10^12) so that bad input returns 409 and not 500.

findings.issue: Repairing a shipment whose SALE has already been booked produces a misleading audit trail. If the DELIVERED event arrives after the report, or two admins repair at the same time with different amounts, recordDelivered does nothing (ON CONFLICT on the SALE). saleBooked() is still true, so the row is marked resolved and its detail says 'repaired with admin-entered amount X', and the INFO log says the same, even though X was never booked. The money is safe because the SALE is unique per shipment, but the record is wrong.
findings.fix: Check saleBooked(d.shipmentId()) before posting. If a SALE already exists, either resolve the row with detail 'already booked (amount <booked>)' and leave out the entered amount, or return 409. Write the amount actually booked, read back from ledger_entries, into detail and the log.

findings.issue: signum() is checked before rounding. An amount such as 0.004 passes the check, is rounded to 0.00 by recordDelivered, and books SALE 0.00, COMMISSION 0.00 and FEE -10.00, so the seller ends up 10.00 down and the discrepancy is marked resolved.
findings.fix: Round to scale 2 (HALF_UP) first, then require the rounded value to be > 0. Pass the rounded value on to recordDelivered.

findings.issue: The UNMATCHED_REVERSAL repair calls reverseReturn(d.orderId(), ...). When the SALE belongs to a different order, the new order_id guard throws IllegalArgumentException. That is not an ApplicationException, so the repair returns 500, the WARN 'refused for <actor>' line is skipped, and condition 7 (failed repairs logged with the actor) is not met on this path. Nothing is posted, so money is safe.
findings.fix: In post(), catch IllegalArgumentException from reverseReturn and rethrow it as a ResourceConflictException, for example 'Reversal names another order than the SALE', so the caller gets 409 and the WARN line is written.

findings.issue: Abuse and availability: POST /api/admin/ledger/reconcile runs the whole job on the HTTP request thread and makes one Feign call to order-service per SALE from the last 35 days, one after another, with nothing to stop it early. With order-service down, each call can take up to about 4 s (1 s connect plus 3 s read), so a run can hold its advisory-lock connection for hours. During that time the nightly run is skipped and the request times out at the gateway. A FINANCE user can also trigger a full sweep of order-service again and again. This does not lock out a payout run: the page reads take no row locks, the job lock has a different name from the payout run's, and the payout run's FOR UPDATE is never blocked by these reads.
findings.fix: Stop the STATE_MISMATCH Feign loop after N consecutive FEIGN_ERRORS (and record that in the counts), and consider running the manual trigger asynchronously (return 202) or rate-limiting it, for example one manual run per hour.

summary: All six part-A minors are fixed at d811b88. (1) reverse() now selects order_id under FOR UPDATE and throws IllegalArgumentException on a mismatch, which is not retried, so the event goes to the DLT. A test covers it. (2) The claim of no deadlock is now limited to a single shipment, in the LedgerService comments and in td-p9-22, which records the multi-shipment payout deadlock and its fix. (3) The LEDGER ALERT log prints only presence flags plus the parsed BigDecimal, and returnId and returnShipmentId must parse as UUIDs. The test checks that 'FORGED' does not appear in the log. (4) The repair no longer books the register amount: MISSING_SALE requires ?amount=, and without it returns 409 and books nothing. order-service must confirm DELIVERED and the seller first. The amount and actor are logged and appended to detail. (5) The V4 plain index on ledger_entries(shipment_id) is present. (6) The part-A release gate is satisfied now that the reconciler and repair have landed. New surface: all three /api/admin/ledger endpoints use @PreAuthorize hasAnyRole('ADMIN','FINANCE') behind the anyRequest().authenticated() chain. A test shows ROLE_SELLER gets 403. resolved_by is jwt.getSubject() (a UUID, enforced by UuidSubjectValidator), and the request body is ignored (tested). AuditInterceptor records successful POSTs under /api/admin/. The Feign client is the existing sellerOrderClient with InternalTokenFeignConfig: it sends X-Internal-Token to /internal/orders/shipments/{id} with 1 s connect and 3 s read timeouts. The only extra header is the admin's bearer token, which the existing relay interceptor forwards only to in-cluster targets. All reconciler SQL uses bound parameters. The only concatenation is the constant WHERE in list(), and the grace interval comes from server config. No PII: report rows and logs hold UUIDs, amounts, kind and the order-service status string. ShipmentInfo.userId is never stored or logged. The reconciler cannot lock out a payout run: it reads without row locks and outside any transaction, and its job lock name differs from the payout run's. No new dependency: spring-boot-webmvc-test is test scope only and comes from the catalog. One major finding blocks approval. The admin-entered MISSING_SALE amount has no upper bound, so a single ADMIN/FINANCE user can book an arbitrary SALE up to 10^12 that then flows into the next payout, and the durable audit.events record leaves the amount out because AuditInterceptor drops the query string. Fix: limit the amount to the register value on the row (larger amounts need a separately audited path), and add the amount to the audit event. The remaining minors are a misleading 'repaired with amount' note when a SALE is already booked, rounding a sub-cent amount to a zero SALE that still takes the fee, a 500 with no WARN when an UNMATCHED_REVERSAL repair hits the order mismatch, and no early stop or rate limit on the Feign sweep.
